# Bank Transfer Instruction

Represents one payer-requested bank transfer with separate bank confirmation. It includes `clauses.bankTransferState` to initialize transfer state even before Activation is ready. A transfer request does not establish reserved, secured or transferred money. Only `Payment Completed` with `evidence: bankConfirmation` records transferred money. There is no synthetic card authorization or capture; a refund is a separate transfer instruction.

## Terms and runtime state

`paymentTerms.method` is defined as `bank-transfer`, and `paymentTerms.evidence` as `bankConfirmation`. `paymentTerms.amountMinor` supplies the transfer amount in integer minor units; `paymentTerms.currency` supplies its currency. The transfer request cannot override either. `paymentTerms.payerChannel` and `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel` identify the channels checked for requests and bank responses.

The Bank Transfer State clause has a pointer binding named `state`, defaulting to `/bankTransfer`. Its declared initial values are `status: idle`, `requestId: ""` and `reference: ""`: no transfer request or bank reference has yet been recorded. The transfer functions explicitly read and write `/bankTransfer`; changing the clause binding does not establish that those functions follow another location.

`/bankTransfer/status` distinguishes `idle`, `requested`, `unknown`, `declined` and `completed`. `requested` records an issued request; `unknown` records an unresolved bank outcome. `/bankTransfer/requestId` identifies the transfer request, and `/bankTransfer/reference` holds the recorded bank outcome reference.

Payment-ledger initialization is separate from transfer-state initialization. The inherited initialization step responds to `Initialize Payment`, `Clauses Initialized` and `Document Activated`. It calls the payment initializer only when `/payment/accepted` is absent and either `/clauses/activation` is absent or `/activation/active` is exactly `true`. Initialized transfer structure therefore does not itself establish acceptance or readiness.

All paths refer to the document executing this instruction, including a nested instruction’s own document. Missing runtime values remain unknown; they do not imply the declared initial values, zero amounts or completion.

## Transfer operations

All four transfer entry points first call `requireActive` with the calling channel; its detailed admission rules are not supplied. Every operation requires a nonempty text `requestId` of at most 128 characters. Outcome responses also require a nonempty text `reference` of at most 256 characters.

- **`requestTransfer`** runs on `payer` and accepts only `requestId`. The calling channel must match `paymentTerms.payerChannel`, and `/payment/accepted` must be exactly `true`. If `/clauses/documentSources` exists, `/sourceLinks/ready` must also be exactly `true`. For a new request, `/payment/closed` must not be `true`; if `paymentTerms.transferGate` exists, it names a document path whose value must be exactly `true`. Acceptance writes `/bankTransfer/requestId`, sets `status` to `requested`, and emits a `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Requested`, the request ID, and the amount and currency from `paymentTerms`.
- **`confirmTransfer`** runs on `guarantor` and requires exactly the business fields `requestId`, `reference`, `amountMinor` and `currency`. The amount and currency must exactly match `paymentTerms`; this records confirmation of the full instruction amount, not a partial transfer.
- **`declineTransfer`** and **`reportTransferUnknown`** run on `guarantor`, recording `declined` and `unknown` respectively. They require `requestId` and `reference`; `amountMinor` and `currency` are optional. Those optional details are neither checked against the terms nor persisted by the shown recorder, and do not update completed money.

All bank responses require the calling channel to match `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel` and the supplied request ID to match an already recorded, nonempty `/bankTransfer/requestId`. Only `requestId`, `reference`, `amountMinor` and `currency` are accepted as outcome business fields; an additional explanation field is not part of these inputs. Invalid identifiers, references, extra fields, authority mismatches, request mismatches and confirmation amount or currency mismatches reject the operation.

Once a transfer request ID is recorded, a different ID is rejected. Repeating the same ID returns `duplicate` without issuing another request, including after a final outcome. Source readiness, payer authority and acceptance checks still apply to that retry; the closed-payment and transfer-gate checks occur only for a new request.

A new outcome may replace `requested` or `unknown`. Thus an unknown outcome can later be reconciled as completed or declined against the same request. Repeating the current outcome requires the same reference and returns `duplicate`; a different reference for that same outcome is a conflict. Confirmation retries must still supply the matching amount and currency. `completed` and `declined` reject changes to another outcome. A change from `unknown` to a different outcome may record a new reference.

Each newly recorded outcome updates `status` and `reference` and emits a `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Outcome`, `requestId`, `reference` and `status`. Completion additionally sets `/payment/completed` to the full `paymentTerms.amountMinor`, sets `/payment/transactionId` to the bank reference, and emits `Payment Completed` with `amountCompleted`, `evidence: bankConfirmation`, `reference` and `requestId`. Declined and unknown outcomes do not perform these completion updates. The return value `acceptedNew` means a new request or outcome was recorded; it does not by itself mean money transferred.

## Inherited payment and clause behavior

The inherited `guarantor` operation `acceptPaymentInstruction` accepts an empty object or optional text `reason`; `rejectPaymentInstruction` requires a nonempty `reason`. `recordTransactionInitiated` requires a nonempty `transactionId` without `/` or `~`. Its optional `initiatedAmount` defaults during execution to `paymentTerms.amountMinor`; `attachmentPoint`, `providerReference` and `railType` are optional transaction details.

Other inherited payment entry points submit successful securing, completion, cancellation and reversal responses through `secureFunds`, `completePayment`, `cancelBeforeCompletion` and `reverseAfterCompletion`, with related operations for declined, failed and unknown outcomes. Control responses cover final amount resolution, payee assignment, transaction details, and completion, reversal and transaction-detail-update locks. These request-based responses identify a recorded request in `payment.requests` or `payment.controlRequests` using a nonempty `requestId`. Optional financial assertions named `amount`, `amountMinor`, `amountSecured`, `amountCompleted` and `amountReversed` must each equal the recorded request amount when supplied. Declared rejection, failure and unknown response inputs require a nonempty `reason`. The shared payment-function bodies are not supplied, so their complete eligibility rules and ledger effects are not established here; their presence does not establish bank confirmation.

The inherited clause host installs configuration and processes amendment proposals. It rejects preexisting `/clauseRuntime` during initialization, concurrent amendments, stale `expectedRevision` or `expectedConfigurationId`, malformed changes and duplicate clause keys. Changes support `add`, `update`, `replace` and `remove`; additions require a new key, while other actions require an existing key. Clause keys must be nonempty and contain neither `/` nor `~`. Candidate clauses require `type`, object-valued `parameters` and `bindings`, and the required validation and planning hooks. Existing clauses participate in transition validation unless `transitionUnconditional` applies. An amendment request is not an installed configuration: `Amendment Accepted` identifies a material, fully installed transition. Available operations establish neither a personal obligation nor the current reader’s permission to invoke them.
